newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Price rise makes MOL gas sales profitable - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Price rise makes MOL gas sales profitable - analyst.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt's share of the recent gas price increase should bring MOL's gas business out of the red, an analyst said on Monday.
Gas wholesale prices will increase by 16.9 percent, according to the official gazette Magyar Kozlony.
"This increase would give MOL an about two percent margin on its gas sales," said Rudi Voros, London-based analyst of ICE Securities.

The government announced last month that it would raise retail gas prices to domestic consumers by 18.8 percent and electricity prices by 24.9 percent on January 1, but it left the Ministry of Industry and Trade to work out margins for suppliers and distributors

Laszlo Pal, MOL's chairman was quoted by the national daily Magyar Hirlap as saying he finds the company's share of the price increase "correct", but he said he could only give a more exact assessment after the first quarterly adjustment of the price next April.
Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt, which still holds 60 percent of MOL said earlier it will sell a further 12 to 18 percent stake in the company next year.
MOL director for capital markets Zoltan Aldott said earlier this month that if MOL's share was near the total gas price hike it would result in "a substantial swing in operating profitability".

In the first nine months of 1996 MOL imported 5.5 billion cubic meters of natural gas which it sold at state-regulated prices at a loss of 2.4 forints (1 cent) per cubic metre, the company said in October.
Voros said that MOL now has the added benefit of having replenished its gas reserves ahead of the price increase.
He added that the company "had lobbied successfully for its share in the price rise", although Pal said that in his capacity as a member of Hungary's parliament he did not lobby for the company.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed on Monday at 2,005 forints, down 10.
However, brokers said this is not a worrying sign.

"This was not a typical bourse day," said Attila Gazdik of New York Broker. "MOL shares have been on a slow but constant rise, as opposed to a surge after which the danger of a correction is higher." ($ = 161.4 Hungarian Forints)
